title: Why and when is preventive maintenance necessary?
summary: Bennie Schamp, Senior Director Service Poultry at JBT Marel, discusses the importance of preventive maintenance, which is increasingly being recognized by more processors. “Over the years, a lot has changed regarding equipment and the market. With higher line speeds and longer production times, reactive service is no longer sufficient. More and more customers are therefore opting for preventive maintenance schedules. Preventive maintenance focuses on the timely replacement of critical parts to keep machines performing stably at a high level and to reduce the risk of unexpected downtime.”
body_markdown:
#### The switch to preventive maintenance


Bennie Schamp: “The market has changed significantly over the past 15 to 20 years. When we started with preventive maintenance, only a few customers were interested. Most processors still had time for maintenance in the evenings and weekends and did not see the necessity. But with increasing line speeds and production hours, the risk of failures and production stops increases exponentially. Additionally, there is little time left for maintenance. No wonder more and more processors are choosing a preventive maintenance schedule, with machine checks and parts replacement based on time intervals rather than inspections.”
